faq.q: What is the origin of Medina?
faq.a: Medina is associated with Arabic. Medina is Arabic مَدِينَة (Madīna) 'city', and specifically the city of the Prophet in Arabia. The source gloss 'City of the Prophet' is broadly consistent. Recorded as a place name also used as a given name.
Yes — the underlying form مدينة is Arabic.
Medina can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Medina mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Medina is rendered مدینہ and carries the sense مدینہ، عرب کا شہر.

faq.q: What does Medina mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Medina is rendered مدینه and carries the sense مدینه، شهری در عربستان.
A romanized syllable approximation is me-di-na. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Medina?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Medina, medina. Script forms are مدينة, مدینه, مدینہ, मदीना.

faq.q: Is Medina a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
